assumptions.condition: \(F_1,\ldots,F_n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P^F\).
Under \(P^F\), enabling at \(a\) makes treatment active in every period \(t\ge a\).

Under \(P^F\), for every \((g,e)\in\mathcal A_\omega\) and \(c\in\mathcal J_{g,e}\), \(E_{P^F}[Y_{i,g+e}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,b_g}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=g,S_i=1,X_i]-E_{P^F}[Y_{i,g+e}(\infty,1)-Y_{i,b_g}(\infty,1)\mid G_i=c,S_i=1,X_i]=E_{P^F}[Y_{i,g+e}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,b_g}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=g,S_i=0,X_i]-E_{P^F}[Y_{i,g+e}(\infty,0)-Y_{i,b_g}(\infty,0)\mid G_i=c,S_i=0,X_i]\).
Every eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_\omega(X_i)\) lies in \([\underline\kappa,\overline\kappa]\) almost surely.

novel.justification: Finite strata and smooth conditional covariance models with noncollinear clean-comparison shocks have a fixed positive spectrum bound.

assumptions.condition: The observable operator \(A_P\) has closed range and \(A_PA_P^*\) is boundedly invertible on \(\mathcal C_P\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).

novel.justification: For finite covariate strata this is ordinary full-rank conditional DDD moment design; for smooth designs it is a stable completeness-style restriction on the observable four-cell residual system.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), the deterministic bases have envelopes at most \(r_n^{-1}\), \(L_n+J_n=o(n)\), population sieve Grams are uniformly conditioned, and the coefficient, score, propensity, outcome, and covariance surfaces have sieve approximation bias at most \(r_n\).

novel.justification: Finite-stratum indicator dictionaries and compact Hölder classes with spline dictionaries meet these law-level approximation and conditioning requirements.

assumptions.condition: The deterministic off-fold learners in Definition 3 satisfy uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_n\) the displayed empirical-process, nuisance-product, covariance, and ridge approximation bounds with common envelope \(r_n\), where \(r_n\to0\), \(\delta_n\to0\), and \(\sqrt n r_n^2\to0\).

novel.justification: The rate statement is score-specific. Finite strata give parametric entrywise rates; Hölder-sieve least squares and multinomial likelihood give the stated joint envelope after dimension selection.

definitions.name: Population DDD projection candidate
definitions.construction: Form the observable centered residual vector \(U_\omega\), set \(A_Ph=\Sigma_\omega^{-1}E_P[U_\omega h\mid X_i]\), \(A_P^*v=U_\omega^{\prime}v(X_i)\), set \(q_P=m_\omega-\tau_\omega\), and form \(\widetilde\varphi_\omega=q_P-A_P^*(A_PA_P^*)^{-1}A_Pq_P\).

definitions.name: Off-fold executable sieve-Riesz construction
definitions.construction: On \(I_k^c\), choose \(\widehat p_{-k}\) as the lexicographically first minimizer of clipped multinomial negative log likelihood over the simplex sieve generated by \(B_n\); choose each \(\widehat\mu_{-k}\) and each entry of \(\widehat\Sigma_{-k}\) as the lexicographically first least-squares sieve minimizer for respectively \(\Delta_{g,e}Y\) and \(\widehat U_{\omega,-k}\widehat U_{\omega,-k}^{\prime}\). Set \(\widehat\Sigma^{\mathrm{reg}}_{\omega,-k}=\Pi_{\mathrm{PSD}}((\widehat\Sigma_{-k}+\widehat\Sigma_{-k}^{\prime})/2)+\lambda_{\Sigma,n}I_{q_\omega}\), \(\widetilde S_{n,-k}=S_n-\mathbb P_{-k}S_n\), \(\widehat G_{-k}=\mathbb P_{-k}[(B_nB_n^{\prime})\otimes\widehat\Sigma^{\mathrm{reg}}_{\omega,-k}]+\lambda_{G,n}I\), \(\widehat C_{-k}=\mathbb P_{-k}[(B_n\otimes I_{q_\omega})\widehat U_{\omega,-k}\widetilde S_{n,-k}^{\prime}]\), \(\widehat d_{-k}=\mathbb P_{-k}[\widetilde S_{n,-k}\widehat m_{-k}]\), and \(\widehat b_{-k}=\widehat G_{-k}^{-1}\widehat C_{-k}(\widehat C_{-k}^{\prime}\widehat G_{-k}^{-1}\widehat C_{-k}+\lambda_{R,n}I)^{-1}\widehat d_{-k}\). Define \(\widehat\Pi_{T,-k}f=\widetilde S_{n,-k}^{\prime}[\mathbb P_{-k}(\widetilde S_{n,-k}\widetilde S_{n,-k}^{\prime})+\lambda_{T,n}I]^{-1}\mathbb P_{-k}[\widetilde S_{n,-k}f]\) and \(\widehat a^0_{-k}=-\widehat\Pi_{T,-k}[(B_n^{\prime}\otimes\widehat U_{\omega,-k}^{\prime})\widehat b_{-k}]+\mathbb P_{-k}\widehat\Pi_{T,-k}[(B_n^{\prime}\otimes\widehat U_{\omega,-k}^{\prime})\widehat b_{-k}]\). Every inverse is ridge-defined; if a stated unregularized display is needed, use the fixed Moore--Penrose minimum-norm tie rule.

definitions.name: \(\widehat\tau_{\omega,\mathrm{EIF}}\)
definitions.construction: Use \(\widehat\psi_{-k}(O_i;\vartheta)=\widehat m_{-k}(O_i)-\vartheta+\widehat a^0_{-k}(O_i)\), whose slope in \(\vartheta\) is \(-1\), and set the unique fold-averaged root \(\widehat\tau_{\omega,\mathrm{EIF}}=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_k}[\widehat m_{-k}(O_i)+\widehat a^0_{-k}(O_i)]\). Set \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_k}\widehat\psi_{-k}(O_i;\widehat\tau_{\omega,\mathrm{EIF}})^2\).

statements.justification: It supplies the observable common-moment reduction supporting the efficiency problem.
statements.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish this pairwise identification; here it is only supporting structure.

statements.statement: In the fixed observed-data model \(\mathcal M\), the regular observed-data tangent-score space equals \(\ker(A_P)\). For every regular submodel score \(h\in\ker(A_P)\), the four eligibility-by-cohort algebra from consistency, no anticipation, no ineligible spillover, and pairwise conditional DDD trends gives \(\dot\tau_\omega(h)=E_P[q_Ph]\), with \(q_P=m_\omega-\tau_\omega\). The closed-range condition yields a unique projection coefficient \((A_PA_P^*)^{-1}A_Pq_P\); directly, \(E_P[\widetilde\varphi_\omega h]=\dot\tau_\omega(h)\) and \(E_P[\widetilde\varphi_\omega]=0\). Hence \(\varphi_\omega^{\star}=\widetilde\varphi_\omega\) is the canonical gradient and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=E_P[\{\varphi_\omega^{\star}(O_i)\}^2]\) is the semiparametric efficiency bound.
statements.justification: This is the missing field-tier observed-data efficiency bound.
statements.gap: Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie derive a staggered-DiD projection. This strictly tightens its scope by deriving the eligibility-by-cohort DDD derivative, the treated target-share term, and the covariance induced by shared DDD comparison units.
statements.consumer: It is the information benchmark for efficient staggered DDD event studies.

statements.statement: For fixed \(K,T,\mathcal A_\omega\) and common \(B,\varepsilon,\underline\kappa,\overline\kappa\), the deterministic off-fold construction obeys the derived uniform remainder \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_n}P_P(|\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\omega,\mathrm{EIF}}-\tau_\omega)-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\varphi_\omega^{\star}(O_i)|>\zeta)\to0\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_n}P_P(|\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)|>\zeta)\to0\). On subfamilies with bound uniformly positive, Wald coverage converges uniformly to \(1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The field bound needs an executable learned shared-covariance implementation.
statements.gap: Canonical DDD cross-fitting does not cover staggered shared-comparison covariance; generic DML is not used as a proof of this score-specific theorem.

statements.statement: For \((g,e)\in\mathcal A_\omega\) with \(|\mathcal J_{g,e}|\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{g,e}\) holds if and only if \(a_{g,e}^{0}=a_{g,e}^{\star}(X_i)\) almost surely. Moreover \(E_P[(a_{g,e}^{0})^{\prime}\Sigma_{g,e}(X_i)a_{g,e}^{0}-(\mathbf1^{\prime}\Sigma_{g,e}(X_i)^{-1}\mathbf1)^{-1}]=E_P[(a_{g,e}^{0}-a_{g,e}^{\star}(X_i))^{\prime}\Sigma_{g,e}(X_i)(a_{g,e}^{0}-a_{g,e}^{\star}(X_i))]\), strictly positive exactly when \(\mathcal P_{g,e}\) fails.
statements.justification: It gives an exact non-tautological equality frontier for constant GMM.
statements.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna optimize only constant GMM weights. This theorem strictly tightens that restricted optimum by the conditional-GLS equality and loss formula.

statements.statement: Set \(T=3,g=2,e=0,\mathcal G=\{2,3,\infty\},\mathcal A_\omega=\{(2,0)\},\omega_{2,0}=1\), \(P^F(X_i=0)=P^F(X_i=1)=1/2\), and \(P^F(G_i=a,S_i=s\mid X_i)=1/6\). Set \(\theta=0\), \(Y_{i1}(a,s)=Y_{i3}(a,s)=0\), and \(Y_{i2}(a,s)=Z_i\) for all \(a,s\). Conditional on \((G_i,S_i,X_i)\), \(Z_i=0\) except in \((3,1)\) and \((\infty,1)\); there it is equiprobably signed with magnitudes \(\sqrt6/6,\sqrt{24}/6\) in cell \((3,1)\) at \(X_i=0,1\), and \(\sqrt{24}/6,\sqrt6/6\) in cell \((\infty,1)\) at \(X_i=0,1\). Then \(U_{2,0}=R_{2,0}=-6Z_i(\mathbf1\{G_i=3,S_i=1\},\mathbf1\{G_i=\infty,S_i=1\})^{\prime}\), \(\Sigma_{2,0}(0)=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)\), \(\Sigma_{2,0}(1)=\operatorname{diag}(4,1)\), \(a_{2,0}^{0}=(1/2,1/2)^{\prime}\), \(a_{2,0}^{\star}(0)=(4/5,1/5)^{\prime}\), \(a_{2,0}^{\star}(1)=(1/5,4/5)^{\prime}\), and the exact average loss is \(9/20\).
statements.justification: It realizes strict loss under a nondegenerate full-data DDD law.
statements.gap: Published staggered-DDD GMM theory does not quantify this conditional-precision witness.
statements.consumer: It supplies a simulation calibration and diagnostic.

statements.statement: Can the theorem-derived canonical gradient be simplified to a cellwise closed form that retains every shared-unit covariance entry? Handle: sequentially residualize the eligibility-by-cohort coordinates and solve the population normal equations block by block.
statements.justification: A closed form would improve interpretability without presupposing score existence.
statements.gap: Neither sequential-moment geometry nor staggered-DiD formulas include this DDD eligibility/shared-comparison projection.
statements.consumer: It provides an interpretable efficient score.

sampling_model.design: i.i.d. fixed-\(T\) balanced panels generated under \(P^F\) and observed through \(P\)
sampling_model.overlap: positive propensity in every active eligibility-by-cohort cell
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: deterministic off-fold likelihood and least-squares sieves with PSD covariance and separate ridge levels

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: It identifies staggered-DDD group-time ATTs from clean cohorts and minimizes variance over constant GMM combinations.
It derives conditional-covariance-efficient influence functions for overidentified staggered two-way DiD.
It gives an efficient influence function for canonical panel DDD.
It presents transparent stacked DDD that trades efficiency for pairwise interpretation.

tldr: Clean comparison cohorts create an overidentified staggered-DDD residual system whose comparison units and outcome histories are shared. The project derives the fixed-model canonical gradient by a fully typed observable Hilbert projection of the four-cell DDD residual derivative and treated target-share derivative, implements its finite-sieve off-fold approximation with learned shared covariance, and gives an exact frontier for constant-weight GMM.

project_justification.gap: Existing staggered DDD gives pairwise identification and constant GMM, not the full observed-data efficiency bound or executable learned shared-covariance estimator.
project_justification.niche: The model combines the eligibility contrast absent from staggered DiD, cohort overidentification absent from canonical DDD, and cross-cell dependence from reused comparison units.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a field-tier DDD projection, a deterministic sieve implementation, and a primitive constant-GMM loss frontier.

related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025) provide the pairwise staggered-DDD and constant-GMM benchmark that Theorem 3 strictly tightens. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025) inform the conditional-covariance geometry, while Theorem 1 adds the DDD eligibility-by-cohort derivative, target-share derivative, and shared-comparison covariance. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, arXiv v3) provide the already-published canonical panel-DDD score used only for validation. Ai and Chen (2012) motivate the conditional-moment Hilbert architecture. Chernozhukov et al. (2018) inform cross-fitting but do not establish the score-specific covariance-learning theorem. Hsieh (2026) is a transparent stacked-DDD alternative, not a bound comparator.
technical_internal_limitation: Unnumbered validation diagnostic: on the two-period, two-cohort, singleton-aggregate submodel \(T=2,\mathcal G=\{2,\infty\},\mathcal A_\omega=\{(2,0)\},\omega_{2,0}=1\), direct algebra reduces the derived score to the published panel-DDD efficient-influence-function formula in Akbari--Kiyavash--Ghassami (2025, arXiv v3). This is an exact published-result sanity check, not a contribution.
honest_scope: The horizon, aggregate support, and residual dimension are fixed. The proposal excludes unbalanced panels, repeated cross-sections, data-adaptive aggregation weights, singular conditional covariance, and violations of conditional DDD trends. Closed-form cellwise simplification remains open after the population score is derived.
message: Reordered \(L_n\), \(J_n\), and \(k\) before their dependent symbols; JSON and all symbol-reference ordering checks pass.
